disclaimer: All verdicts are drafts from public documentation and need a hands-on creative-director test before publishing. No test results, quotes, stats or testimonials are included.

tools.name: Recraft
tools.good_for: Generates true editable vector (SVG) marks and icon sets, with custom brand styles.
tools.verdict_status: draft: editorial call from public docs, pending creative-director hands-on test
tools.rationale: It's one of the few generators that hands you real vectors instead of a PNG you have to retrace, which is what a logo job actually needs. Treat outputs as sketches to refine in Illustrator, not finished marks.
tools.price: Free (public, non-commercial); Basic $10/mo, Pro $16/mo, Teams $18/seat/mo (billed annually). API from $0.08 per vector image.
tools.notes: Free-plan images are public and not licensed for commercial use.

tools.name: Ideogram
tools.good_for: Image generation with reliable in-image text: wordmarks, posters, type-led social graphics.
tools.verdict_status: draft: editorial call from public docs, pending creative-director hands-on test
tools.rationale: When the job lives or dies on legible type, it's the generator to start with. Expect raster output, so a wordmark still needs vectorizing and kerning by hand.
tools.price: Free 30 credits/week (Google/Apple/Microsoft sign-in); Plus $20/mo ($15 annual), Pro $60/mo ($42 annual), Team $30/user/mo ($20 annual).

tools.name: Looka
tools.good_for: Template-driven logo maker that sells logo files and brand-kit templates to small businesses.
tools.verdict_status: draft: editorial call from public docs, pending creative-director hands-on test
tools.rationale: It's built for founders who don't have a designer, not for designers. You'd be paying $65 for a starting point that's weaker than a 20-minute sketch.
tools.price: Free to design and preview; Basic logo $20 one-time (one low-res PNG); Premium $65 one-time (hi-res + vector); Brand Kit $96/yr.
tools.notes: Pricing confirmed via Looka help page and a third-party summary; open looka.com/pricing to check before publishing.

tools.name: Midjourney (V7 images)
tools.good_for: Art-directed image generation with strong aesthetics, style and omni references.
tools.verdict_status: draft: editorial call from public docs, pending creative-director hands-on test
tools.rationale: Still the fastest way to explore a look before you commit to a shoot or an illustrator. No API and a public gallery unless you pay for Pro, so budget for Pro on client work.
tools.price: Basic $10/mo, Standard $30, Pro $60, Mega $120 (20% off annual). No free tier. Stealth (private) mode Pro+ only.
tools.notes: Midjourney's terms require Pro or Mega for companies with more than $1M gross revenue a year (per plan docs); check the ToS before publishing.

tools.name: Midjourney Video
tools.good_for: Animates a Midjourney still into short clips (SD 480p; HD 720p on Standard+).
tools.verdict_status: draft: editorial call from public docs, pending creative-director hands-on test
tools.rationale: Fine for a moodboard, but it's image-to-video only with low resolution and short clips, so it can't stand in for a client deliverable. Use a dedicated video tool.
tools.price: Included in Midjourney plans; uses GPU time (batch of 4 SD clips is about 8 min, HD about 26 min).
tools.notes: Skip covers client video use only, not the image product.

tools.name: Adobe Firefly
tools.good_for: Adobe's generative suite (image, video, vector, Generative Fill), plus partner models (Gemini, GPT Image, FLUX, Ideogram, Runway, Kling) in one place inside Creative Cloud.
tools.verdict_status: draft: editorial call from public docs, pending creative-director hands-on test
tools.rationale: If you already live in Photoshop and Illustrator, it's the least disruptive way to add generative work to client ads. Adobe's own Firefly models are the conservative pick for commercial use. Partner models carry their own terms, and some aren't available on business plans yet.
tools.price: Free tier; Standard $9.99/mo (2,000 credits), Pro $19.99, Pro Plus $49.99, Premium $199.99. Standard generations are unlimited on paid plans; premium/partner features use credits.
tools.notes: Plan prices are from a third-party summary (saascrmreview.com); check adobe.com/products/firefly/plans before publishing.

tools.name: Krea
tools.good_for: Real-time generation canvas, multi-model image and video, upscaling and custom training.
tools.verdict_status: draft: editorial call from public docs, pending creative-director hands-on test
tools.rationale: The real-time canvas is a real ideation tool for art directors. But it's an aggregator of other labs' models, so quality depends on whichever model you pick. We'll retest once we've run it on a full brief.
tools.price: Free 100 units/day; Basic $9/mo, Pro $35/mo, Max $105/mo, Business $200/mo (about 40% off annual).

tools.name: Canva AI (Magic Studio)
tools.good_for: Brand-kit-aware templates, Magic Resize, and AI generation/editing for high-volume social sets.
tools.verdict_status: draft: editorial call from public docs, pending creative-director hands-on test
tools.rationale: For a 6-to-60 post social calendar with a brand kit, nothing in-house moves faster. Use it for production and resizing, not for concepting the brand itself.
tools.price: Free plan; Pro US$144/yr per person (US pricing, Sept 2026); AI use limits by tier (Premium/Ultra AI uses).
tools.notes: Canva changed Pro pricing and free AI limits in Sept 2026; check exact AI-use counts on canva.com/pricing.

tools.name: Google Pomelli
tools.good_for: Google Labs experiment that reads your website for a 'Business DNA' and generates on-brand social campaigns and ad assets.
tools.verdict_status: draft: editorial call from public docs, pending creative-director hands-on test
tools.rationale: It's interesting because it pulls brand context automatically. But it's a Labs experiment aimed at small businesses, not designers, and its output control is limited. We're watching to see if it leaves Labs.
tools.price: Free (Google Labs experiment); availability limited by country.
tools.notes: The official URL pomelli.withgoogle.com comes from Google's blog; check that it loads.

tools.name: AdCreative.ai
tools.good_for: Generates and 'scores' ad creatives at volume from a brand kit.
tools.verdict_status: draft: editorial call from public docs, pending creative-director hands-on test
tools.rationale: Reviews keep saying the output is generic, and the 'conversion score' is a claim we can't verify. Credit pricing gets steep fast, and trial-billing complaints are common. Designers get better variants from Firefly or Canva with real art direction.
tools.price: Trial 7 days / 10 credits; plans from $39/mo (20 credits) up to $999/mo; discounts on quarterly/annual billing.
tools.notes: Pricing comes from a third-party (competitor) blog. Check adcreative.ai/pricing directly. Don't quote any review stats.

tools.name: Figma Make
tools.good_for: Prompt-to-prototype/app inside Figma, using your design files as context.
tools.verdict_status: draft: editorial call from public docs, pending creative-director hands-on test
tools.rationale: Great for clickable prototypes from existing frames, and it's already in a tool your team pays for. Generated code and layouts still need a designer's cleanup, and the AI credits can run out quickly on big iterations.
tools.price: Included with Figma Full seats (Professional plan about 3,000 AI credits/mo per Full seat); extra credits sold separately.

tools.name: Framer (Wireframer + Workshop)
tools.good_for: Designer-grade site builder with AI page generation (Wireframer), AI components (Workshop), and hosting.
tools.verdict_status: draft: editorial call from public docs, pending creative-director hands-on test
tools.rationale: It ships a real, responsive, hosted site that a designer fully controls, which most 'AI website builders' don't. Wireframer gives you a starting layout, and the craft stays with you.
tools.price: Free (one-time 500 AI credits); Basic $10/mo, Pro $30/mo per site (annual).

tools.name: Runway
tools.good_for: Gen-4.5 / Gen-4 video, Aleph editing, references, 4K upscale, plus third-party models (Kling, Seedance, Nano Banana).
tools.verdict_status: draft: editorial call from public docs, pending creative-director hands-on test
tools.rationale: It's the most complete production toolkit for short-form brand video, with editing and consistency controls beyond plain text-to-video. Credits go fast, so prototype in Turbo first.
tools.price: Free 125 one-time credits; Standard $12/mo, Pro $28/mo, Max $76/mo (annual). Gen-4.5 is 12 credits/sec.
tools.notes: The Unlimited plan is being retired; legacy subscribers move to Max on Nov 30, 2026.

tools.name: Kling AI (Kling 3.0)
tools.good_for: Text/image-to-video with native audio, multi-shot, up to 4K.
tools.verdict_status: draft: editorial call from public docs, pending creative-director hands-on test
tools.rationale: Its motion quality competes with the best. But first-month promo pricing and enterprise data questions mean we'd check the terms before putting client footage in. Adobe currently restricts Kling to individual plans only.
tools.price: Free basic tier; Standard $8.80/mo, Pro $32.56/mo, Premier $80.96/mo, Ultra $159.99/mo (lower intro first month).

tools.name: Google Flow (Veo 3.1)
tools.good_for: Google's filmmaking app on Veo 3.1: scene builder, ingredients-to-video, native audio.
tools.verdict_status: draft: editorial call from public docs, pending creative-director hands-on test
tools.rationale: Veo's realism and audio are strong. But Flow's credit costs scale steeply at Quality, and the best tier sits behind a $100+ Ultra plan. We want to see how consistent it is across a whole campaign.
tools.price: Google AI Pro $19.99/mo (1,000 Flow credits); Ultra from $99.99/mo; Veo 3.1 Quality is 100 credits per generation.
tools.notes: Ultra $99.99 tier came from search synthesis; check one.google.com before publishing.

tools.name: Topaz Studio (Gigapixel / Photo / Video)
tools.good_for: AI upscaling, denoise, sharpen and video enhancement, local and cloud.
tools.verdict_status: draft: editorial call from public docs, pending creative-director hands-on test
tools.rationale: It's the finishing step for low-res AI output, and Adobe itself now licenses Topaz upscalers inside Photoshop. A subscription bundle has replaced perpetual licenses, so price it per project.
tools.price: Studio $69/mo, or $45/mo on an annual commitment, or $399/yr; Studio Pro $799/yr (full commercial use).
tools.notes: Check whether the commercial-use terms on the base Studio tier cover client work.

recipes.title: On-brand social post agent
recipes.tested: PENDING: outline only, not yet tested
steps: Store the brand kit (voice doc, palette hex, fonts, logo SVG, 5 approved reference posts) in a Google Drive folder or Notion page
n8n Schedule trigger (weekly) reads the content calendar rows from a Google Sheet
Claude node writes each post's caption + image prompt, with the voice doc and references as system context; JSON output
HTTP node calls Ideogram (text in image) or Recraft (brand style ID) to generate 2 options per post
Approval gate: send options to Slack/email with approve/reject buttons (n8n Wait node, webhook resume); a human must approve
On approve, upload to Buffer via API as a scheduled post; write status back to the Sheet

recipes.title: Ad variant generator
recipes.tested: PENDING: outline only, not yet tested
tools: Recraft API (style ID, remove background, outpaint) or Adobe Firefly Services API (enterprise)
steps: Input: one approved hero concept (image + headline + CTA) dropped in a Drive folder
Claude generates N headline/CTA variants within character limits per placement
Image API outpaints/extends the hero to each aspect ratio (1:1, 4:5, 9:16, 1.91:1)
Code node composites type and logo with sharp/ImageMagick from a fixed template (no AI-rendered type)
Contact sheet sent for creative-director approval; approved files exported with placement-named filenames
recipes.notes: Firefly Services API is enterprise-only; check access before listing it as the default.
